study.question: Why did feedback compression for auxiliary tasks lower click AUC even when click retained uniform summaries? In g2-r0002-uniform_feedback versus g2-r0002-uniform_uniform, click changed 0.65741931 to 0.65584726 (-0.00157206) while auxiliary mean AUC rose 0.85235211 to 0.86471388 (+0.01236177). The same auxiliary-route factor in g2-r0002-feedback_feedback versus g2-r0002-feedback_uniform changed click by -0.00135429 and auxiliary mean by +0.01217372. Can restricting auxiliary ownership of the shared scorer and/or embeddings retain the useful summaries without that predictive tradeoff?
study.hypothesis: Provisional explanation, not controlled support: feedback-stratified auxiliary readout changes updates to shared local-activation parameters and embeddings, coupling compression quality across tasks even with distinct forward views. A 2x2 backward-routing intervention at the same UF forward operator can locate those update paths. Gradient isolation may recover click quality, but auxiliary quality can also decline; success requires measuring both. Earlier trajectories constrain this choice: g2-r0000-uniform10 achieved click 0.65757059 versus baseline-din 0.65554408 with lower model-batch p50 (9.107 versus 15.254 ms), while its auxiliary mean was lower (0.85425242 versus 0.86138316). g2-r0000-match20 did not beat g2-r0000-rotated20 or simple uniform variants for click, so target-match selection has no click support here. Round1 true feedback groups improved auxiliary AUC against rotated membership while losing click; action conditioning did not eliminate that tradeoff. Round2 UF did not deliver the proposed click/auxiliary compromise. All these are single-seed local observations, not independent repetitions or proof of interference.

study.proposed_difference: Two binary gradient gates define four standalone cells. S blocks auxiliary-loss gradients into shared scorer parameters, while preserving derivatives through scorer inputs. E detaches all auxiliary context, target and compressed value tensors, preventing auxiliary gradients into the embedding table through both direct and scorer paths. Both gates together leave auxiliary towers trainable while shared representations learn from click. Each training forward first scores all30 slots normally, updating persistent Dice state once, then scores the same30 slots through torch.func.functional_call with the same parameters (optionally detached) and cloned buffers. Inference shares the first scorer output and is identical across switches at equal weights/state. This adds zero learned parameters; no new optimizer, loss weighting or training schedule is introduced.
predictions: Prerequisite rather than a scientific result: at identical weights/input/state, all four cells have matching training predictions and persistent buffer updates, and matching evaluation predictions. open_grad also matches the one-call g2-r0002-uniform_feedback forward and gradients to declared FP32/BF16 tolerances. Gate S zeros auxiliary-only scorer parameter gradients without zeroing scorer input/embedding derivatives; gate E zeros all auxiliary-only embedding gradients without blocking scorer parameter or auxiliary tower gradients.

If auxiliary updates through scorer parameters drive the click penalty, scorer_only should improve click AUC relative to open_grad; the embedding gate should provide a smaller additional effect. Reverse ordering supports embedding-mediated coupling; a non-additive response supports interaction of update paths.

Full isolation both_blocked should improve click AUC relative to open_grad if removing auxiliary updates helps the click representation under this frozen recipe. A click recovery of at least0.0010 is a predeclared practical lead, not a significance threshold. Retain auxiliary mean AUC within0.003 of open_grad to call it a useful compromise; otherwise record a quality tradeoff. Do not infer gains from mean four-task AUC.

The SxE interaction is AUC(both_blocked)-AUC(scorer_only)-AUC(embedding_only)+AUC(open_grad). Report it descriptively with the two paired main contrasts; this seed alone cannot establish statistical support. Evaluate all four task AUC/Logloss, click history slices with existing sample/positive/negative counts, parameters, cost, peak memory, throughput and p50/p95.

At equal checkpoint/state, inference uses the same one-pass 30-slot operator for every cell. No expected inference savings between cells; any measured training-time difference must be reported separately from compression savings against full-history DIN.
falsifiers: Any failure of source/init/forward/state parity or isolated-gradient routing invalidates attribution: record the failed check and cost, repair and prospectively resubmit before interpreting training results.

If neither single gate nor both gates recovers click relative to the new open_grad comparator, the proposed detrimental shared-update explanation is unsupported by this intervention. This does not refute all task-specific compression or all implementations of gradient control.
If improvement appears only relative to historical g2-r0002-uniform_feedback but not open_grad, attribute the difference to implementation/numerical changes or variation, not the gates.

If click recovery costs more than0.003 auxiliary mean AUC, the claimed joint compromise is not supported even if the gradient path affects click. If auxiliary ranking changes without a click recovery, record that outcome separately.

If later authorized paired repetitions reverse the sign or paired user-cluster uncertainty includes zero, retain only preliminary or unresolved support. Failure to beat g2-r0000-uniform10 leaves it the incumbent by the primary criterion.
alternative_explanations: Stopping auxiliary gradients removes both helpful and harmful signal; improved AUC alone does not establish angular gradient conflict, causal information loss, or originality.

Gradient routing changes optimization and total gradient magnitude; frozen global dense clipping can couple updates even across otherwise separate task towers. Auxiliary towers still train; embeddings/scorer still evolve from click.

Forward arithmetic is duplicated during training and gradients sum in a different order than the historical one-call implementation. BF16 rounding can diverge across a full pass; the new open-gradient cell is the primary implementation-matched comparator.
Identical parameter capacity and forward operator do not imply identical backward work; report actual allocated GPU/wall seconds, processed examples, peak memory and inference latency.
Single frozen seed and adaptive validation selection are exploratory; auxiliary labels are category/brand associations and official_offline feedback may be immature at prediction time.
Irreversible information loss inside feedback-stratified arithmetic summaries, or loss of a useful auxiliary regularizer, can dominate rather than harmful shared updates.

BatchNorm couples valid/empty summary positions and both views in the forward operator. This is inherited and fixed here; the gates do not test normalization design or prove that forward normalization coupling is harmless.

Useful gradients can be removed along with harmful ones; a later capacity-matched private adapter or independent scorer could retain auxiliary adaptability, but is not included in this zero-capacity intervention.

No local raw parquet, GPU or training framework is present. The successful host receipts establish the starting reference, not a new checksum/loader reproduction in this coding environment. No current held-out outcomes, personal knowledge or cross-task campaigns are used.

cost_plan.attribution_reserve: Budget all four cells, all prerequisites, diagnostics, failed attempts and retries. Before any training, host must verify torch.func availability; matching state-dict keys/shapes and identical initial tensors; parameter totals expected32060453/dense267237; FP32/BF16 train/eval parity at common state; open_grad gradient equivalence to ancestor (sparse gradients coalesced for comparison); isolated auxiliary-only and click-only gradient paths; four finite [B,1] probabilities and total BCE/backward; finite empty/all-invalid, length1, partial-block and full histories; masked ID/action and masked task-mask perturbation invariance; current target-action invariance; persistent BN buffers updated only once. Compare buffers and loss gradients on cloned model states, never sequentially mutated reference states. Host chooses and records tolerances before those checks. Reserve16 trial caps (~19254s) for checks, discriminating follow-up and later host-authorized paired repetitions of consequential cells; this is a resource reserve, not permission to change the frozen training seed in configs. Actual clipping frequency, if available through the authorized host, is diagnostic; no scorer or resource contract modification.
